A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BLISS research work. Their text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original BLISS pretraining results and component ablations, including Tables 1–7. Appendix D distinguishes borrowed baseline results from the work's own evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original BLISS evaluations and adds runtime/memory measurements, optimization-step comparisons and domain-reweighting results in Appendices H–J.

M1.justification: The core BLISS pipeline, KL alignment and LLaMA reset procedure remain unchanged. Appendix J adds a domain-reweighting adaptation whose upper level learns domain weights and uses them for sampling, extending the original sample-scoring and top-ranked selection procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix J extends coverage beyond C4 sample selection to domain-mixture learning on SlimPajama-6B, covering books, scientific papers, code and several web domains. This introduces a distinct evaluated selection task and broader training-data coverage; the original downstream benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The new proxy-fidelity experiment compares proxy-based reweighting against bilevel reweighting that directly optimizes the target LLaMA-300M, with random selection also shown in Figure 9. Comparator membership in the existing C4 experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The original C4 evaluation protocol is retained. New protocols include a 90%/10% training/validation split, 1,000 bilevel steps and LLaMA-134M/300M configurations with test-loss evaluation in Appendix J, a 3,000-versus-5,000-step comparison, and runtime/peak-memory measurement in Appendix H.

E4.justification: Appendices H–J substantially extend the supporting analyses with resource scaling, optimization-budget sensitivity and direct tests of proxy fidelity through domain weights and resulting test losses. Conversely, v1's upper-level validation-loss curves for rounds 2 and 5 are removed; their training curves and the no-KL analysis remain.

E5.justification: Table 8 changes its uncertainty description from standard deviations to standard error, aligning it with Table 1. The uncertainty values are unchanged, and neither additional repeated runs nor new seed counts or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Appendices H–J add resource measurements, optimization-loss comparisons and domain-weight/test-loss findings. Table 10 reports BLISS/MATES selection times of 5.03/18.0 hours at 410M and 11.82/30.32 hours at 1B, with higher BLISS peak memory. Main benchmark accuracies remain unchanged, but Tables 1 and 8 correct BLISS's 1B FLOPs from 8.08 to 19.53 × 10^19, matching the value already present in v1 Table 4.

T1.justification: Equation (2) moves weight decay outside the batch summation, eliminating the extra batch-size factor in the printed update. Equation (5) adds the required gradient transposes, and Algorithm 2 removes an erroneous reassignment in the GDLS recurrence. The underlying bilevel formulation and implicit-gradient derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain from-scratch bilevel data selection without external pretrained oracles, accounting for long-term influence, and improved pretraining efficiency. The headline 1.7× speedup and 1.4-percentage-point improvement in the 2.8B experiment are retained.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges higher peak memory from Hessian-vector products, replacing the conclusion's planned visual/multimodal extension with this practical limitation. It also interprets the new experiments as supporting 3,000-step sufficiency and proxy fidelity, while retaining the existing KL-alignment explanation.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies Adam updates using the calculated hypergradient; this documents implementation without establishing an optimizer change between runs. Table 9 corrects learning-rate symbols and revises batch-size disclosure. Appendix J supplies a dataset locator and settings for the new experiment.

R1.justification: Related work adds Meta-rater, ALInfIK, token-wise influential-data retrieval and a short description of QUAD; Adam and SlimPajama references are also added. The central positioning relative to MATES and SEAL remains. Publication and bibliographic updates to existing references do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections, clarifies upper/lower-level terminology, expands algorithm comments and optimizer explanations, and condenses the author/affiliation block. Appendices H–J are appended, while the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 10 and new Figures 8–10, combines the retained round-2/5 training panels into Figure 6 while dropping their validation panels, and renumbers the existing no-KL figure as Figure 7. Table 5 moves from the main text to Appendix C, with additional figure grouping, caption and placement revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a limited net improvement through corrected FLOP, uncertainty and algorithm reporting, measured runtime–memory tradeoffs, and new optimization-budget and proxy-fidelity checks. These make methodological and efficiency claims easier to assess. The main benchmark evidence remains unchanged, and removing the round-2/5 validation-loss curves reduces transparency about upper-level optimization.
